headline: A roundup of AI travel-planning mistakes tells of hikers sent to a Peruvian canyon that does not exist and of a traveller stranded by wrong visa advice.
score_reason: Lowered from 2 to 1: a branded roundup that retells mostly older, undated cases.
importance_line: Travellers who rely on chatbots for itineraries can lose money or be stranded if they do not check the details, but the cases are retold from earlier reports and most are undated in this roundup.
summary: A roundup produced by Bodog and distributed by Stacker, carried by Vancouver Is Awesome, retells cases of AI travel advice going wrong, including two hikers in Peru sent to a "Sacred Canyon of Humantay" that does not exist, as a local guide told the BBC, and an Australian author reportedly left stranded in Mexico City after ChatGPT's visa advice for Chile. Its advice is to check every part of an AI-made itinerary yourself, and it gives no dates for most of the cases, which come from earlier reports rather than new events.
notes: Read from fulltext on Vancouver Is Awesome (url). Branded roundup by Bodog via Stacker; the original Bodog page was not found. Old cases retold: editor may hold it as stale. Score lowered 2 to 1.
